summary.text: Donna A. Lupardo, first elected in 2005, represents the 123rd Assembly District, which includes the City of Binghamton and the Towns of Vestal and Union.
Her official biography says she chairs the Assembly Agriculture Committee, a post she has held since 2019.

paragraphs.text: Originally from Staten Island, Lupardo graduated from Wagner College and moved to the Southern Tier in 1976 to attend graduate school at SUNY Binghamton, where she received a master's degree.

She stayed on as a lecturer in the School of Education and Human Development for ten years before turning to community mental health education and public service, and served on the Broome County Legislature from 1999 to 2000.
The biography says she is the first woman to represent Broome County in the State Legislature.
In the Assembly she became chair of the Committee on Children and Families in 2013, the Committee on Aging in 2017 and the Committee on Agriculture in 2019.

She also serves on the Economic Development, Higher Education, Rules, Steering and Transportation Committees, co-chairs the New York Legislative Aviation Caucus, and has chaired the bipartisan Legislative Women's Caucus.
Her biography lists legislation she has seen signed into law, including the Safe Drinking Water Schools Act, the Work-Zone Safety Act and the Industrial Hemp Pilot Program.
She lives in Endwell with her husband, Scott J. Peters, a Cornell University professor.
